limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: Adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 and for the fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed in any supplied document. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA and all adjusted leverage and cover ratios are therefore not established, and the revenue chart leaves the fourth quarter of 2025 blank on that measure. The fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 earnings release would close it. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18 - High: Trailing reported EBITDA is negative, so total and net debt to EBITDA and cumulative leverage in the debt stack are not calculable for 2026-09-30. The impairment-excluded measure is an analyst figure and is labelled as such; it restricts conclusions to the impairment alone. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C10 - Medium: The term loan's springing maturity depends on a liquidity test defined in an agreement that was not supplied, and the clause names Senior Secured Notes while the issuer has Senior Unsecured Notes. The maturity ladder is drawn at stated final maturities and could place 149.6 in 2028 instead of 2031. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 23 - Medium: Scheduled amortization of the term loan is not stated; one repayment of 0.4 was made in 2026, so the zero entries for 2026 and 2027 in the maturity ladder follow stated final maturities only. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22 - Medium: Revolver availability is the lesser of the commitment and a borrowing base the issuer does not print; undrawn capacity equal to the commitment is as stated by the issuer. The delayed draw term loan is excluded from liquidity because its secured leverage condition cannot be tested. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 55 - Medium: Guarantor scope and security for the Senior Unsecured Notes are not stated in the sources read, so the notes are ranked from their unsecured description only; collateral and guarantor lists for the term loan and revolver are not named. Executed documents would be needed for any priority or recovery conclusion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 19–25 - Low: Instrument-level carrying values are not printed; a single financing cost adjustment of -6.6 reconciles principal to the Debt line, with 5.2 identified for the term loan and 1.4 for the notes by difference. Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 19 - Low: Source dashes are retained as missing, not zero: impairment of long-lived assets in the nine-month and quarter 2025 columns and the 2026 quarter, repayment and issuance lines in the cash flow statements, and several lines printed in only one of the annual and quarterly statements. Totals still reconcile in every column. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7 - Low: Purchase commitments of USD 474.8 million and fixed lease payments of USD 16.9 million are stated only at 2025-12-31; they are not updated at 2026-09-30 and are outside Total Debt, as are operating lease liabilities of USD 6.0 million and the warrant liability of USD 9.2 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 205; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 29 - Low: Total interest expense net of interest income is printed only for 2026 and 2025 interim periods, so annual EBITDA uses the gross interest expense line and the bridge carries a 2.6 interest income step; the depreciation and amortization figure differs by 0.1 between the cash flow statement and the release. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17 - Low: Fourth-quarter 2025 revenue, net income and operating cash flow are derived by difference because no fourth-quarter report was supplied; the figures are labelled calculated and are not used in any ratio. Basis: calculation C11 - Low: Covenant levels (a total leverage ratio not above 5.25 to 1.00 tested quarterly from 2026-09-30, and a secured leverage ratio not above 1.75 to 1.00 for the delayed draw) are stated by the issuer with compliance at 2026-09-30, but their EBITDA definitions are not supplied, so no covenant headroom is calculated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–24

facts.label: T2D.9 - Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: The risk level is driven by shareholder repurchases and looser covenants alongside steady debt reduction, because cash to equity and added debt capacity compete with deleveraging, which implies a moderately adverse effect on creditors. facts.text: Revenue is driven by government option exercises and by naloxone price and volume. The government is a monopsony buyer with unilateral termination rights, and its ACAM2000 option exercises fell from USD 120.0 million in 2023 to USD 99.9 million in 2024 and USD 56.0 million in 2025, which shows declining order value rather than pricing power. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Trailing earnings no longer cover Emergent's debt: reported EBITDA for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 is USD -106.6 million, so leverage is not calculable and creditors rely on cash, liquidity and the 2028 maturity date rather than earnings cover.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7

The loss comes from a USD 191.3 million impairment of the NARCAN intangible asset and a fall in third-quarter revenue to USD 110.0 million from USD 231.1 million. Before the impairment, trailing EBITDA is USD 84.7 million and net debt of USD 332.0 million is 3.92x that figure, an analyst measure the issuer does not report.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 16

Debt has fallen from USD 663.7 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 507.7 million at 2026-09-30 after the April 2026 refinancing and USD 75.0 million of note repurchases. Cash of USD 175.7 million and an undrawn USD 50.0 million revolver give liquidity of USD 225.7 million, and the USD 364.7 million 2028 notes are the next maturity.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 55

### Financial interpretation

Earnings, not the balance sheet, are the weak point. Revenue for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 is USD 649.1 million against USD 1,043.6 million in FY2024, the NARCAN franchise is losing price and volume to generic and branded competitors, and that deterioration triggered the second-quarter impairment that turns trailing reported EBITDA negative. Leverage on that measure is therefore not calculable, and the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA of USD 127.5 million for nine months 2026 is 38% below the USD 204.8 million of a year earlier.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64

The strongest offset is cash. Operating cash flow was USD 200.1 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow USD 188.4 million, helped by a USD 62.6 million inventory release that will not repeat, and the issuer retired USD 75.0 million of notes and USD 150.0 million of prior term loan in 2026. If trailing EBITDA excluding the impairment of USD 84.7 million is the right earnings base, net debt is 3.92x, which is high for an issuer whose quarterly Adjusted EBITDA was negative in Q3 2026; the next quarters of revenue and margin are the test.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 7

Liquidity is adequate but narrower than a year ago. Cash of USD 175.7 million plus the undrawn USD 50.0 million revolver is USD 225.7 million, down from USD 305.4 million at 2025-12-31 because the revolver commitment was halved and cash fell after the milestone payment, note repurchases and refinancing costs. The USD 75.0 million delayed draw term loan is not counted because drawing it needs secured leverage no higher than 1.75x under a definition that is not supplied, so availability cannot be tested.
Basis: calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 55

Maturities are concentrated in 2028. The USD 364.7 million notes fall due on 2028-08-15 and, on the issuer's own earlier presentation of a similar clause, the USD 149.6 million term loan could spring forward to 2028 if more than USD 75.0 million of notes remain and a liquidity test is unmet; the revolver already springs to 2028-05-17 while notes remain. Each note repurchase therefore shortens the exposure as well as reducing debt.
Basis: calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 191

Deferred revenue is a small but rising non-debt funding source: the balance of USD 14.3 million at 2026-09-30 compares with USD 5.0 million at 2025-12-31 in the re-presented comparative, while inventories fell from USD 343.4 million to USD 280.9 million. Customer advances fund operations until the associated deliveries are made, so lower advance receipts would remove a source of cash at the same time as the inventory release runs out.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29

A supported downside sequence starts with further erosion of NARCAN pricing or volume in U.S. public-interest channels, which cuts Commercial Products margin first, then reported EBITDA and trailing cover, and finally the ability to meet the term loan's total leverage covenant of 5.25x tested from the quarter ended 2026-09-30. The issuer states compliance at 2026-09-30; the covenant is not computed here because its EBITDA definition is not supplied. Observable triggers are quarterly Naloxone revenue, government order timing and the next compliance statement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44

## Findings
### Bottom line

Emergent is now a government-dependent credit: U.S. government biodefence orders, not naloxone, carry the cash flow that services its debt, so order timing and a finance-chief handover matter more to creditors than any sponsor behaviour, because no sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified.
Basis: calculation C03; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 156–157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 28

The government supplied 55.36% of revenue in nine months 2026 against 45.37% a year earlier, while naloxone revenue fell 26.05% and led to a USD 191.3 million impairment. Management cut debt principal by USD 185.7 million since 2024-12-31 and spent USD 18.1 million on share repurchases in nine months 2026, and the issuer describes the April 2026 refinancing as bringing less restrictive covenants.

Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; EX99.1_2026-03-31_ebs_a04162026refinancingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Key findings

- Government concentration is the central business risk, and it is rising. The U.S. government supplied 55.36% of revenue in nine months 2026 against 45.37% in nine months 2025; its long-term contracts expire between 2026 and 2036 and can be terminated or modified unilaterally, and orders arrive through annual options, so total revenue swung from USD 234.3 million in Q2 2026 to USD 110.0 million in Q3 2026. Creditors are exposed to the timing of option exercises more than to end demand.

Basis: calculation C03; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 156–157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX99.1_2026-06-30_ebs_ebs202606-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The naloxone franchise has stopped diversifying the business. Naloxone revenue fell 43.32% in FY2025 and 26.05% in nine months 2026 as generic competitors and an unfavourable price and volume mix in U.S. public-interest channels cut sales, which led to the USD 191.3 million impairment of the NARCAN intangible asset; the franchise is now 27.74% of revenue, so the commercial engine no longer offsets government timing.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50

- Financial policy is creditor-aligned on debt but mixed on equity. Debt principal fell from USD 700.0 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 514.3 million at 2026-09-30 through a USD 100.0 million voluntary prepayment and USD 85.3 million of note repurchases, yet the company also repurchased USD 24.9 million of shares in 2025 and USD 18.1 million in nine months 2026 while earnings weakened, and the term loan carries an uncommitted incremental facility of the greater of USD 200.0 million and 80% of covenant EBITDA, which the issuer says increases its ability to incur more debt.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 187–189; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 26

- There is no sponsor, so creditors face neither sponsor extraction nor a sponsor equity backstop, and the filings identify no controlling shareholder. The company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, ownership percentages sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the only lender link to the equity is warrants equal to 4.86% of shares outstanding, whose exercise prices sit above the USD 8.44 average paid for shares in July 2026.
Basis: calculation C08; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 217; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

- Management is in the middle of a turnaround with a leadership handover, and the legal overhang is mostly resolved. The finance chief retires on 2026-12-31 with an interim successor from 2027-01-01, while the August 2026 plan cuts about 90 employees, around a tenth of the workforce, for targeted annualized savings of about USD 40.0 million; the securities class action settled for USD 40.0 million with insurers funding USD 30.0 million, the derivative case brought USD 15.0 million from insurers, and a Department of Justice discussion continues.

Basis: calculation C09; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 208–211; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX99.1_2026-06-30_ebs_ebs202606-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

- The manufacturing footprint is being rationalised, which lowers fixed cost but raises reliance on third parties. The Baltimore-Bayview plant was sold for about USD 36.5 million at closing, the Camden drug product plant went to Bora, Rockville was closed and the services business is no longer a reportable segment, while most products depend wholly or partly on third-party manufacturers, some as sole source.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 62
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the durability of government demand and the pace of debt reduction. Remaining performance obligations were USD 241.9 million at 2026-09-30, USD 222.7 million of it recognizable within 24 months, new orders continued (a CYFENDUS modification of about USD 24 million in August 2026 and a BioThrax order of up to USD 22.3 million on 2026-11-04), and principal debt is USD 185.7 million lower than at 2024-12-31.
Basis: calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_a1142026biothraxmodpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

The view would soften if naloxone revenue stopped falling for consecutive quarters, if government orders were spread more evenly through the year, or if the share repurchase authorization of USD 37.3 million remaining were left unused while the 2028 notes stay outstanding. It would harden on the non-exercise of a major government option, a further impairment, a covenant waiver or amendment, or a debt-funded distribution.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 26
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so ownership percentages, board independence and executive pay are not established; the finding that no controlling shareholder exists rests only on what the annual and quarterly reports state and could change if a large holder is disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 217

- The executed financing agreements were not supplied, so how much creditor protection the April 2026 refinancing removed cannot be measured; the loosened-covenant finding rests on the issuer's own description of the new terms.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_ebs_a04162026refinancingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–25

- Contract values and expiry dates are disclosed for only some government contracts, so revenue visibility beyond the remaining performance obligations is not established and the concentration trend may reflect option timing rather than a lasting shift.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 14–19

- The restructuring headcount and savings are management estimates revised between the second and third quarter reports, so the cost-cutting offset to the naloxone decline is unproven until reported results show it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 14

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The April 2026 refinancing replaced the prior term loan with a USD 150.0 million term loan from OrbiMed, adds a USD 75.0 million delayed draw term loan available for 24 months subject to a secured leverage condition, and cuts the asset-based revolving commitment from USD 100.0 million to USD 50.0 million; both facilities now mature on 2031-04-16, subject to springing earlier maturities. The issuer describes the terms as less restrictive covenants with more capacity to incur incremental debt, and the term loan allows an uncommitted incremental facility of the greater of USD 200.0 million and 80% of covenant EBITDA. For creditors this extends the maturity wall past the 2028 notes but loosens the protection around them.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_ebs_a04162026refinancingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–23

Alongside the refinancing, the company repurchased USD 75.0 million principal of its 3.875% Senior Unsecured Notes for USD 68.1 million of cash in the third quarter of 2026, leaving USD 364.7 million due on 2028-08-15, after repurchasing USD 10.3 million in 2025 and prepaying USD 100.0 million of the prior term loan in December 2025. No new notes were issued in the period covered by the documents.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 187–189

## Findings
### Bottom line

Emergent presents a weak credit profile: earnings are deteriorating and trailing reported EBITDA is negative, so creditors rely on USD 225.7 million of liquidity and government orders to reach the USD 364.7 million notes due in 2028, and refinancing is the decisive risk.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C08; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash generation is better than earnings, with USD 200.1 million of trailing operating cash flow, but it was helped by a USD 62.6 million inventory release in nine months 2026. Net debt of USD 332.0 million is 3.92x trailing EBITDA before the impairment, an analyst measure, and the issuer's reported fair value puts the 2028 notes at 91.47% of principal, which shows stress rather than distress.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Key findings

- The earnings base is the weakest dimension and is still deteriorating. Reported trailing EBITDA is USD -106.6 million after the USD 191.3 million NARCAN impairment, the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 127.5 million for nine months 2026 from USD 204.8 million and was USD -4.6 million in Q3 2026, and the November forecast implies Q4 2026 Adjusted EBITDA between USD -17.5 million and USD 12.5 million. Leverage multiples are therefore not meaningful on reported numbers, and cover turns positive only after the impairment is excluded.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–9

- Cash flow is a real support but is flattered by working capital. Trailing operating cash flow is USD 200.1 million and free cash flow USD 188.4 million, with trailing cash interest of USD 37.6 million, but the net inventory release over the period was USD 76.8 million; without it free cash flow is USD 111.6 million, still 2.97x cash interest, which is adequate cover only while capital spending stays near USD 11.7 million a year.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but thinner than a year ago. Cash of USD 175.7 million and the undrawn USD 50.0 million revolver give USD 225.7 million, down 26.10% from USD 305.4 million at 2025-12-31 because the revolver commitment was halved and cash was spent on notes, a milestone payment and refinancing costs; the issuer states its liquidity is adequate for at least twelve months, and no principal falls due before 2028 on stated maturities.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 55

- Refinancing is the decisive risk and it is concentrated in 2028. The USD 364.7 million notes become current on 2027-08-15 and fall due on 2028-08-15, the revolver springs to 2028-05-17 while they remain outstanding, and the term loan could spring forward if more than USD 75.0 million of notes remain and a liquidity test in the agreement is unmet, which would put all USD 514.3 million of principal in 2028; liquidity covers 61.89% of the notes and 43.88% of all principal today.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The business is concentrated in one customer and one declining franchise. The U.S. government supplied 55.36% of nine-month 2026 revenue, naloxone has fallen to 27.74% of revenue after a 43.32% decline in FY2025, and ACAM2000 option exercises fell from USD 120.0 million in 2023 to USD 56.0 million in 2025, so revenue depends on option timing that management does not control.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Financial policy helps creditors on debt but gives some of it back. Principal fell USD 185.7 million since 2024-12-31 and the term loan margin is 200 basis points lower, worth about USD 3.0 million a year on USD 150.0 million, yet share repurchases continued and the issuer says the new terms are less restrictive with more incremental debt capacity; covenant compliance is asserted but headroom cannot be calculated from the documents supplied.
Basis: calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-03-31_ebs_a04162026refinancingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–24
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is cash and the government order book. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 200.1 million is 5.32x cash interest, remaining performance obligations are USD 241.9 million, principal debt is USD 185.7 million lower than at 2024-12-31, the August 2026 plan targets about USD 40.0 million of annualized savings, and the November forecast raises adjusted gross margin to 45% to 47% from 42% to 44% even as revenue is cut.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 28

The view would improve if Q4 2026 results land near the top of the implied range, with revenue near USD 144.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA near USD 12.5 million, if naloxone revenue stops falling, or if note repurchases bring the outstanding notes below USD 75.0 million, which would remove the term loan's springing clause. It would worsen if Q4 revenue falls toward USD 99.6 million, if operating cash flow turns negative once the inventory release ends, or if the notes are still above USD 75.0 million as the springing dates approach without a refinancing plan.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23
### Limitations

- Covenant headroom and the springing-maturity liquidity test cannot be computed because their definitions are not supplied, so the refinancing view rests on stated maturities, reported liquidity and the issuer's compliance statement and could improve or worsen once the agreements are read.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 20–24

- Leverage is read on trailing EBITDA adjusted for the impairment only, so the reading of 3.92x would change materially if the issuer's own trailing Adjusted EBITDA became available, which would also revise the earnings-weakness finding.
Basis: calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- No ratings, peer set or market quotes beyond the notes' reported fair value were supplied, so the weak assessment is made on absolute metrics rather than against sector peers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- The forward view uses management's 2026 forecast ranges, which were cut at the third quarter and are untested against results, so the implied Q4 ranges bound the outlook only loosely.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is cash generation that exceeds earnings. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 200.1 million against capital spending of USD 11.7 million means debt service does not depend on EBITDA that is depressed by a non-cash impairment, which supports the next twelve months of liquidity and the credit's ability to keep repurchasing notes.
Basis: calculation C04; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second strength is a government order book and a lower debt load. Remaining performance obligations of USD 241.9 million and principal debt USD 185.7 million lower than at 2024-12-31 reduce near-term refinancing need and give some visibility, although option timing remains management's weakest control.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 28; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is the earnings collapse in the commercial franchise. Naloxone revenue is down 43.32% in FY2025 and 26.05% in nine months 2026 on generic competition and price and volume mix, which produced the USD 191.3 million impairment and turns trailing reported EBITDA negative, so creditors cannot lean on leverage multiples.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second weakness is the 2028 maturity cluster. The USD 364.7 million notes, the revolver's springing date and the term loan's conditional springing clause converge in 2028 while liquidity covers 61.89% of the notes, so any further earnings slippage turns a manageable wall into a market-access problem.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23

The third weakness is concentration and loosened protection. Government customers are 55.36% of nine-month revenue, buyback authority of USD 37.3 million remains, and the issuer describes less restrictive covenants and more incremental debt capacity, which weakens the position of noteholders behind secured lenders.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 26
### Company description

Emergent supplies government-procured medical countermeasures (anthrax, smallpox, botulism and Ebola products), naloxone nasal sprays sold over the counter and to public and first-responder buyers, and a shrinking contract manufacturing service. Revenue visibility is mixed: the countermeasure lines run on multi-year contracts with annual options, whereas naloxone competes in open markets. This supports cash-flow visibility for the government lines and weakens it for naloxone, so debt service capacity depends on option timing and on holding the naloxone decline.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9
### Ownership and group structure

Emergent is a listed company with no sponsor and no identified controlling holder, so creditors face no sponsor extraction but also no sponsor equity backstop; the ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. The only lender link to the equity is the warrants issued with the 2024 term loan. Debt sits at the registrant with unnamed subsidiary guarantors, so structural priority cannot be assessed here.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 21–25
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is driven by government option exercises and by naloxone price and volume. The government is a monopsony buyer with unilateral termination rights, and its ACAM2000 option exercises fell from USD 120.0 million in 2023 to USD 99.9 million in 2024 and USD 56.0 million in 2025, which shows declining order value rather than pricing power. Naloxone has no pricing power against generic and branded entrants, so it is cyclical in neither direction but structurally declining in price.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 156; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Manufacturing cost is largely fixed, so lower volumes cut margin directly: nine-month 2026 gross margin was 39% against 48% and the third quarter was 14% against 54%. The August 2026 plan and asset sales lower fixed cost, but plant shutdown costs and absorption losses show margins are not defended under volume pressure, so cost flexibility is limited in the near term.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 52
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity is low, with capital spending of USD 13.8 million in FY2025, and trailing free cash flow of USD 188.4 million exceeded cash interest of USD 37.6 million several times over, but restructuring cash, milestone payments and an inventory release make the conversion lumpy. EBITDA does not convert to cash predictably, which supports debt service in the next twelve months more than it supports deleveraging.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry and entry are the forces that matter. Generic and branded naloxone entrants (Teva, Padagis, Amneal and prescription competitors) cut price and volume, and the government vaccine and antiviral lines face substitutes such as JYNNEOS and TPOXX, so competitive pressure is the main driver of the naloxone decline. Buyer power sits with the U.S. government, which holds unilateral termination rights, and supplier power is high because several products depend on sole-source third-party manufacturers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 62–64
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are material and the other categories are not. The U.S. government may prefer U.S.-made products and reduce purchases of items made in the Winnipeg facility, and government funding appropriations drive option timing, so policy changes feed directly into revenue; interest-rate exposure is small, with a one percentage point rise in the reference rate adding about USD 1.5 million of annual interest.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, page 63
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the licensed government products with few competitors, positive operating cash flow and falling debt. Weaknesses are the negative trailing EBITDA, the naloxone decline, customer concentration and the 2028 cluster. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are the restructuring savings, Canadian and international orders and note repurchases below the springing threshold; threats are further generic erosion, deferred government options and a refinancing window that closes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and diversification are average to weak, with eleven products but two revenue engines and one dominant customer. Margin stability and free cash flow stability are weak and average respectively, cost and capex flexibility is average, liquidity is average, refinancing access is weak until the 2028 cluster is addressed, and financial policy and governance is average because debt reduction is offset by buybacks and looser terms. Trend is down on earnings and flat on liquidity, and the key missing data are the financing agreements and trailing issuer Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months the forecast points to a weak Q4 2026, with implied Q4 revenue of USD 99.6 million to USD 144.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD -17.5 million to USD 12.5 million, then a year in which restructuring savings and government orders must offset naloxone erosion. Tailwinds are preparedness orders, the Canadian standing offer for NARCAN and lower interest cost; headwinds are generic competition, option timing and the 2027 current-maturity date for the notes. Over three to five years the 2028 and 2031 maturities frame the refinancing question.
Basis: calculation C06; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_ebs_ebs202609-30ex99er-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Qualitative downside scenario

The downside starts with a further fall in NARCAN price or volume in U.S. public-interest channels and a deferred government option, which push Q4 2026 revenue toward USD 99.6 million and keep Adjusted EBITDA negative. Fixed manufacturing cost then deepens the margin loss, operating cash flow turns negative once the inventory release ends, cash falls from USD 175.7 million, and the notes become current on 2027-08-15 while trailing EBITDA is still weak. Management levers are the restructuring, asset sales, curtailing buybacks and further note repurchases, but resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis only through 2027; the observable triggers are quarterly naloxone revenue, option exercises and the notes' reported fair value.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ebs.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23
### Overall credit view

Overall, Emergent presents a weak business profile supported by licensed government products and positive cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by negative trailing reported EBITDA, a declining naloxone franchise and customer concentration. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for twelve months but not established beyond that. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Q4 2026 and 2027 order timing, naloxone stabilisation and progress retiring notes. The primary downside path is naloxone erosion plus deferred government orders ahead of the 2028 cluster. Further analysis would require the financing agreements and trailing issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Top risk: refinancing of the 2028 notes.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C08; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
